name: Pulsar timing probes ultralight dark matter
summary: Ultralight scalar ('fuzzy') dark matter has an oscillating pressure that makes the metric potentials oscillate at f=2mc²/h, in the nHz band for m~10⁻²³ eV, leaving coherent PTA residuals. PTAs also bound dark-matter substructure through the Doppler and Shapiro shifts of passing clumps.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)

name: nHz background from supermassive-black-hole binaries
summary: Hierarchical galaxy mergers pair up central black holes into binaries, whose combined inspiral predicts a nanohertz background with h_c∝f^{-2/3}. The amplitude PTAs reported in 2023 constrains SMBH mass functions, merger rates and how binaries get past the final-parsec problem.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Pulsar timing found the first exoplanets
summary: The timing model PTAs use fits pulse arrival times for Rømer delays, spin-down and noise. Applied to PSR B1257+12, it left periodic residuals that Wolszczan and Frail attributed to Earth-mass planets, the first confirmed exoplanets. The same residual analysis now searches for nanohertz gravitational waves.
sources: Wolszczan & Frail (1992). "A planetary system around the millisecond pulsar PSR1257 + 12". *Nature* 355, 145. [doi:10.1038/355145a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/355145a0)

name: Millisecond pulsars as a galactic GW detector
summary: Millisecond pulsars, spun up by accretion in binaries, are clocks stable to ~100 ns over decades. PTAs turn an ensemble of them into a galaxy-sized detector whose arms are pulsar–Earth baselines. Intrinsic spin noise and dispersion-measure variations are the main systematics.
sources: Hewish et al. (1968). "Observation of a Rapidly Pulsating Radio Source". *Nature* 217, 709. [doi:10.1038/217709a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/217709a0)
NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae
summary: A Galactic core-collapse supernova should emit a GW burst from proto-neutron-star oscillations, convection and SASI, with h~10⁻²¹–10⁻²² at 10 kpc. Current detectors reach only the Milky Way. Third-generation detectors such as Einstein Telescope would extend that reach and, alongside the neutrino burst, probe the explosion mechanism.

name: Loop quantum cosmology bounce before inflation
summary: Loop quantum cosmology replaces the big-bang singularity with a bounce at ρ_c≈0.41 ρ_Pl, using an effective Friedmann equation. The bounce sets pre-inflationary initial conditions and can suppress low-ℓ CMB power. These signatures depend on the model and are unconfirmed.

name: Vacuum energy and the cosmological constant problem
summary: Lorentz invariance forces the renormalised vacuum stress tensor into the form ⟨T_μν⟩=−ρ_vac c² g_μν, which gravitates exactly like Λ. Naive estimates of ρ_vac exceed the observed ~6×10⁻²⁷ kg m⁻³, about (2.3 meV)⁴, by up to ~120 orders of magnitude: the cosmological constant problem.
map: \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm vac}=-\rho_{\rm vac}c^2g_{\mu\nu}\ \Rightarrow\ \Lambda_{\rm eff}=\Lambda+\frac{8\pi G}{c^2}\rho_{\rm vac}
sources: Weinberg (1989). "The cosmological constant problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 61, 1. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1)

name: Quantum vacuum fluctuations seed cosmic structure
summary: Inflationary perturbations are QFT on a quasi-de Sitter background. Bunch–Davies vacuum fluctuations of the inflaton and the graviton are stretched beyond the horizon and freeze, becoming the nearly scale-invariant scalar spectrum (n_s≈0.965) and a tensor spectrum set by H/M_Pl.

name: CMB dipole: our motion through the relic radiation
summary: A Lorentz boost turns an isotropic blackbody into a blackbody whose temperature depends on direction. The 3.36 mK CMB dipole implies the Solar System moves at ~370 km/s, and Planck detected the accompanying aberration and Doppler modulation of the small-scale anisotropies. The CMB frame is a cosmological rest frame, not a violation of relativity.

name: Cosmological redshift vs special-relativistic Doppler
summary: At low z the cosmological redshift looks like a Doppler shift with v≈cz, and any FLRW redshift can be built from infinitesimal Doppler shifts parallel-transported along the photon path. The recession velocity in Hubble's law is not a Lorentz velocity, however.
breaks: Recession speeds v=Hd exceed c beyond the Hubble sphere, and z records the expansion between emission and reception, not a relative velocity in one inertial frame. Converting z to a velocity with the SR formula gives wrong distances at z≳0.5.

name: Cosmic-ray muons: time dilation observed
summary: Muons produced by cosmic rays ~15 km up reach sea level only because their 2.2 μs lifetime is dilated by γ~10–50. Rossi and Hall's 1941 measurement of muon flux against altitude was one of the first direct confirmations of relativistic time dilation.

name: Superluminal motion and Doppler boosting in jets
summary: Jet components moving at β≈1 close to our line of sight show apparent transverse speeds up to γβc, observed up to tens of c. Their flux is boosted by a high power of the Doppler factor δ, which is why blazars dominate the extragalactic gamma-ray sky.

name: Threshold kinematics: the GZK cutoff
summary: Cosmic-ray protons above ~5×10¹⁹ eV photoproduce pions on CMB photons. The threshold follows from the invariant s, and at Lorentz factors γ~10¹¹ these losses limit proton horizons to ~100 Mpc, which explains the observed flux suppression.
sources: Greisen (1966). "End to the Cosmic-Ray Spectrum?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 16, 748. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.16.748](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.16.748)

name: Compactness problem demands Γ≳100 outflows
summary: Millisecond GRB variability implies a tiny source, whose MeV photon density would be opaque to γγ→e⁺e⁻. The emitter must move with bulk Lorentz factor Γ≳100: beaming lowers comoving photon energies below pair threshold and enlarges the inferred emission radius by Γ².
sources: Mészáros (2006). "Gamma-ray bursts". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 69, 2259. [arXiv:astro-ph/0605208](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0605208)

name: GRB photon timing bounds Lorentz violation
summary: Quantum-gravity-motivated dispersion, v≈c(1−ξE/E_QG), would delay high-energy photons from cosmological GRBs relative to low-energy ones. Fermi-LAT timing of GRB 090510 pushed the linear-order scale E_QG past the Planck energy.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Early universe as the testing ground for BSM physics
summary: Three cosmological facts need physics beyond the Standard Model: dark matter, the baryon asymmetry and inflation. In the thermal history, interaction rates are compared with the Hubble rate, and this tests BSM masses and couplings against Ω_c, η_B, N_eff and the primordial spectrum.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: Dark matter requires physics beyond the Standard Model
summary: No Standard Model particle can be the astrophysical dark matter, because neutrinos are too light and too hot. Its gravitational evidence is therefore the strongest empirical case for new particles, and each BSM model maps to its own direct, indirect, collider and structure-formation signatures.
sources: Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Misalignment axions as cold dark matter
summary: After the QCD transition, the axion field starts oscillating from a misaligned initial angle, and these coherent oscillations redshift like cold matter. For f_a~10¹¹–10¹² GeV they give the observed density, which ties the strong-CP solution to galactic halos.
sources: Weinberg (1978). "A New Light Boson?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 40, 223. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.223](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.223)
Wilczek (1978). "Problem of Strong P and T Invariance in the Presence of Instantons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 40, 279. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.279](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.279)

name: Ultralight axions as fuzzy dark matter
summary: An axion-like field with m~10⁻²² eV has a kpc-scale de Broglie wavelength, so halos grow solitonic cores with interference granules and small-scale power is suppressed. Lyman-α and dwarf-galaxy kinematics now push m≳10⁻²¹–10⁻²⁰ eV, which squeezes the original small-scale motivation.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)

name: Axion haloscopes as direct detection of wave-like DM
summary: Through the aFF̃ coupling, galactic-halo axions convert to microwave photons inside a magnetised resonant cavity (ADMX, HAYSTAC). The local dark-matter density and the halo velocity dispersion set the signal power and the line width.
sources: Peccei & Quinn (1977). "CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 38, 1440. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440)

name: Stellar energy-loss bounds on light particles
summary: Any light, weakly coupled particle made in a stellar plasma escapes freely and carries energy away. The red-giant-branch tip, horizontal-branch star counts (R-parameter) and white-dwarf cooling bound g_aγγ≲0.66×10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹, g_ae~10⁻¹³ and the neutrino magnetic moment, rivalling laboratory searches.

name: SN 1987A burst duration bounds new particles
summary: SN 1987A's ~10 s neutrino signal shows the proto-neutron star cooled by neutrino diffusion. Extra free-streaming emission of axions, dark photons or sterile neutrinos would have shortened it, which bounds axion–nucleon couplings (m_a≲10–20 meV) and leaves a 'trapping' window open for strongly coupled heavier particles.

name: Solar axions, helioscopes and solar-model limits
summary: Primakoff conversion of thermal photons in the ~1.3 keV solar core makes a keV axion flux, which helioscopes (CAST, IAXO) reconvert to X-rays by pointing a magnet at the Sun. Helioseismology and solar neutrino fluxes independently cap the extra energy loss at about 0.1 L_⊙.

name: Baryon asymmetry: measured by cosmology, explained by BSM
summary: Cosmology measures η_B≈6.1×10⁻¹⁰, and BBN and the CMB agree on it. Particle physics must generate this value through Sakharov's conditions: B violation, C and CP violation, and a departure from equilibrium supplied by the expansion or by a first-order phase transition.
sources: Sakharov (1967; reprinted 1991). "Violation of CP invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe". *Sov. Phys. Usp.* 34, 392. [doi:10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497](https://doi.org/10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497)

name: CMB acoustic peaks measure the baryon asymmetry
summary: Baryon loading changes the relative heights of the odd and even acoustic peaks, which fixes Ω_b h²≈0.0224 and hence η_B≈6.1×10⁻¹⁰. Every baryogenesis mechanism (electroweak, leptogenesis, Affleck–Dine) must reproduce this target, and BBN deuterium cross-checks it independently.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: CMB limits on dark-matter annihilation at recombination
summary: Dark matter annihilating around z~600–1000 injects energy that ionises hydrogen and broadens last scattering. Planck bounds p_ann below 3.2×10⁻²⁸ cm³ s⁻¹ GeV⁻¹, excluding s-wave thermal relics below about 10–30 GeV with no dependence on halo modelling.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: Relic abundance from Boltzmann freeze-out
summary: Thermal relics follow a Boltzmann equation on the FRW background, and annihilation stops once n⟨σv⟩ drops below H at x_f=m/T_f≈20–25. The relic density therefore depends on the expansion rate and g_*: weak-scale ⟨σv⟩ gives Ωh²≈0.12, while freeze-in or non-standard expansion such as early matter domination shifts the answer.
sources: Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Astrophysics brackets the dark-matter mass range
summary: Candidates span about 90 orders of magnitude in mass, and astrophysics sets the edges. Tremaine–Gunn phase-space packing in dwarfs needs fermions heavier than roughly 0.1–1 keV, galaxy-scale de Broglie wavelengths bound bosons from below at m≳10⁻²¹ eV, and microlensing limits compact-object dark matter.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)
Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Astrophysical evidence fixes candidate properties
summary: Rotation curves, cluster lensing, the Bullet Cluster and the CMB require a non-baryonic component with Ω_c h²≈0.12 that is cold or at most warm and collisionless or only weakly self-interacting. Every particle candidate must meet these constraints.
sources: Clowe et al. (2006). "A Direct Empirical Proof of the Existence of Dark Matter". *Astrophys. J.* 648, L109. [arXiv:astro-ph/0608407](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0608407)
Rubin & Ford (1970). "Rotation of the Andromeda Nebula from a Spectroscopic Survey of Emission Regions". *Astrophys. J.* 159, 379. [doi:10.1086/150317](https://doi.org/10.1086/150317)

name: DM microphysics imprinted on small-scale structure
summary: Each candidate leaves its own small-scale mark: warm dark matter free-streams, fuzzy dark matter has a quantum-pressure Jeans scale, and self-interacting dark matter thermalises halo cores. The Lyman-α forest, Milky Way satellites, lensing substructure and stellar streams turn these imprints into bounds on particle mass and cross section.
sources: Tulin & Yu (2018). "Dark matter self-interactions and small scale structure". *Phys. Rep.* 730, 1. [arXiv:1705.02358](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02358)
Bullock & Boylan-Kolchin (2017). "Small-Scale Challenges to the ΛCDM Paradigm". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 55, 343. [arXiv:1707.04256](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.04256)

name: WIMP–nucleus elastic scattering rate
summary: The nuclear-recoil spectrum folds the particle cross section, coherently enhanced as A² for spin-independent couplings, with the local halo density and velocity distribution. Liquid-xenon TPCs (LZ, XENONnT) now exclude σ_SI below 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² near 30–40 GeV.
sources: Goodman & Witten (1985). "Detectability of certain dark-matter candidates". *Phys. Rev. D* 31, 3059. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.31.3059](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.31.3059)
LZ Collaboration (2023). "First Dark Matter Search Results from the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 131, 041002. [arXiv:2207.03764](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03764)

name: Thermal-relic cross section predicts annihilation signals
summary: The ⟨σv⟩≈3×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s that sets the relic density also predicts today's annihilation flux of γ-rays, positrons, antiprotons and neutrinos from dense regions, and Fermi-LAT dwarf limits exclude thermal s-wave WIMPs below about 100 GeV in the bb̄ channel. The Galactic Center excess is a candidate signal, disputed because millisecond pulsars could explain it.
sources: Hooper & Goodenough (2011). "Dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Center as seen by the Fermi Gamma Ray Space Telescope". *Phys. Lett. B* 697, 412. [arXiv:1010.2752](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.2752)
Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Cosmological-constant and Higgs-mass naturalness
summary: Both are UV-sensitivity problems of effective field theory. Vacuum-energy corrections scale as Λ_UV⁴ against an observed (2.3 meV)⁴, just as Higgs-mass corrections scale as Λ_UV², and the same remedies (SUSY, extra dimensions, relaxation, anthropic selection) are tried on both.
breaks: TeV-scale SUSY or compositeness can cancel δm_H², but no known symmetry cancels vacuum energy while letting SUSY be broken. The cosmological-constant problem is still ~60 orders of magnitude off with a TeV cutoff, and it involves gravity directly.
sources: Weinberg (1989). "The cosmological constant problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 61, 1. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1)
Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)

name: GUT monopole problem motivated inflation
summary: Breaking a simple GUT group down to a subgroup containing U(1)_em leaves nontrivial π₂ of the vacuum manifold. The Kibble mechanism then makes about one monopole per horizon volume, enough to overclose the universe, and Guth designed inflation partly to dilute them. GUT-scale vacuum energy remains a natural inflation scale, with V^{1/4}≲1.4×10¹⁶ GeV from r<0.036.
sources: Guth (1981). "Inflationary universe: A possible solution to the horizon and flatness problems". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 347. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347)
Georgi & Glashow (1974). "Unity of All Elementary-Particle Forces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 32, 438. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438)

name: Collider vs direct-detection complementarity
summary: In simplified-mediator and Higgs-portal models the same couplings set both LHC missing-energy rates (mono-jet, invisible Higgs decays with BR<0.107) and nuclear-recoil rates. Collider limits therefore map onto the σ_SI–m_χ plane and dominate below a few GeV, where recoils are too soft to detect.
sources: ATLAS Collaboration (2012). "Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC". *Phys. Lett. B* 716, 1. [arXiv:1207.7214](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.7214)

name: LHC data calibrate air-shower hadronic models
summary: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays collide at √s≈430 TeV per nucleon pair, so reading composition from X_max and muon counts means extrapolating hadronic models (EPOS-LHC, Sibyll, QGSJET) tuned at the LHC, including forward LHCf data and the 2025 oxygen runs. The observed muon excess in air showers, the 'muon puzzle', points to mismodelled forward hadron production.

name: Cosmic rays as particle physics's first beam
summary: Before accelerators, cloud chambers and emulsions exposed to cosmic rays revealed the positron (1932), the muon (1936), the pion (1947) and strange particles. The detector lineage now runs the other way: collider-style silicon trackers, calorimeters and magnetic spectrometers fly as AMS-02, DAMPE and Fermi-LAT.

name: Pion decay links neutrinos, γ-rays and cosmic rays
summary: Accelerated hadrons hitting gas or photons make pions. Charged pions decay to neutrinos with E_ν≈E_p/20 and neutral pions to γ-rays with E_γ≈E_p/10, so decay kinematics tie the neutrino, γ-ray and cosmic-ray fluxes of TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane together.
sources: IceCube Collaboration et al. (2018). "Multimessenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident with high-energy neutrino IceCube-170922A". *Science* 361, eaat1378. [arXiv:1807.08816](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.08816)
IceCube Collaboration (2023). "Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane". *Science* 380, 1338. [arXiv:2307.04427](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04427)

name: Neutrino astronomy runs on particle-physics neutrinos
summary: Neutrino telescopes need particle-physics inputs: cross sections, oscillation parameters and flavour identification. In return they supply natural beams at TeV–PeV energies and Mpc–Gpc baselines that no accelerator reaches, which test oscillations, neutrino decay and Lorentz invariance.
sources: IceCube Collaboration (2013). "Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector". *Science* 342, 1242856. [arXiv:1311.5238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238)

name: Neutrino fog: CEvNS in dark-matter detectors
summary: Coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering, first observed by COHERENT, gives nuclear recoils that look like WIMP recoils. Solar ⁸B neutrinos mimic a ~6 GeV WIMP and atmospheric and DSNB neutrinos set a 'fog' that slows sensitivity gains; XENONnT and PandaX-4T reported first ~2.6–2.7σ indications of ⁸B CEvNS in 2024.

name: Water-Cherenkov detection scaled to km³ telescopes
summary: IceCube, KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD reuse the Kamiokande/Super-K water-Cherenkov technique at gigaton scale in ice or sea water. The same detectors treat atmospheric neutrinos as background for astronomy and as signal for oscillation physics (DeepCore, ORCA).
sources: IceCube Collaboration (2013). "Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector". *Science* 342, 1242856. [arXiv:1311.5238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238)
Super-Kamiokande Collaboration (1998). "Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 81, 1562. [arXiv:hep-ex/9807003](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ex/9807003)

name: pp-chain and CNO neutrinos test stellar fusion
summary: Hydrogen burning makes stars neutrino sources, and the measured pp, ⁷Be, ⁸B and CNO fluxes confirm the stellar energy source directly. Neutrino energy losses (plasma, pair and Urca processes) drive late stellar evolution.
sources: SNO Collaboration (2002). "Direct evidence for neutrino flavor transformation from neutral-current interactions in the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 89, 011301. [arXiv:nucl-ex/0204008](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-ex/0204008)
Woosley, Heger & Weaver (2002). "The evolution and explosion of massive stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1015. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015)

name: Core-collapse supernova neutrinos
summary: About 99% of the ~3×10⁵³ erg released in core collapse leaves as neutrinos of all flavours over ~10 s. Kamiokande-II, IMB and Baksan caught about 25 events from SN 1987A, confirming the picture, and Super-K-Gd, JUNO, DUNE and IceCube now await a Galactic burst and the diffuse supernova neutrino background.
sources: Woosley, Heger & Weaver (2002). "The evolution and explosion of massive stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1015. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015)

name: Solar neutrinos and the standard solar model
summary: Solar neutrino fluxes from Homestake to Borexino tested the standard solar model, and SNO showed the deficit came from flavour conversion, not from the model. Helioseismology independently confirmed the model's sound-speed profile, and Borexino's CNO flux now probes the solar metallicity problem.
sources: SNO Collaboration (2002). "Direct evidence for neutrino flavor transformation from neutral-current interactions in the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 89, 011301. [arXiv:nucl-ex/0204008](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-ex/0204008)
Christensen-Dalsgaard (2002). "Helioseismology". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1073. [arXiv:astro-ph/0207403](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0207403)

name: CMB bounds on the sum of neutrino masses
summary: Massive relic neutrinos turn from radiation into matter after recombination, which changes the early ISW effect and the CMB lensing potential. Planck bounds Σm_ν below about 0.12 eV, which complements the model-independent kinematic tritium bound from KATRIN.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)
KATRIN Collaboration (2022). "Direct neutrino-mass measurement with sub-electronvolt sensitivity". *Nature Phys.* 18, 160. [arXiv:2105.08533](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.08533)

name: Neutrino free-streaming suppresses matter clustering
summary: Relic neutrinos do not cluster below their free-streaming scale, so small-scale matter power drops by ΔP/P≈−8f_ν. With BAO fixing the expansion history, DESI DR1 plus CMB gives Σm_ν<0.072 eV (95%), pressing against the 0.059 eV minimum for normal ordering.
sources: DESI Collaboration (2025). "DESI 2024 VI: Cosmological Constraints from the Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations". *JCAP* 02, 021. [arXiv:2404.03002](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03002)

name: Astrophysical neutrino flavour ratios
summary: Over cosmic baselines oscillations average out, so a pion-decay source ratio of 1:2:0 arrives at Earth as about 1:1:1. IceCube's measured flavour composition, including ν_τ candidates and a Glashow-resonance event near 6.3 PeV, tests the source mechanism and new physics such as neutrino decay or Lorentz violation.
sources: IceCube Collaboration (2013). "Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector". *Science* 342, 1242856. [arXiv:1311.5238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238)

name: Collective neutrino flavour conversion in supernovae
summary: Near a proto-neutron star, ν–ν forward scattering makes flavour evolution a nonlinear many-body problem, with spectral swaps and fast flavour instabilities. These may change neutrino heating behind the shock and r-process conditions, but how much they matter for the explosion is unresolved.

name: MSW resonance in the solar density profile
summary: Coherent forward scattering on solar electrons adds the potential √2 G_F n_e, so ⁸B neutrinos cross the resonance adiabatically and leave as ν₂ with P_ee≈sin²θ₁₂≈0.3. Low-energy pp neutrinos keep the vacuum-averaged P_ee≈0.55, and Borexino measured the transition between the two.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

SNO Collaboration (2002). "Direct evidence for neutrino flavor transformation from neutral-current interactions in the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 89, 011301. [arXiv:nucl-ex/0204008](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-ex/0204008)

name: N_eff limits on light sterile neutrinos
summary: An eV-scale sterile neutrino with the mixing suggested by the LSND, MiniBooNE and gallium anomalies would be thermalised before BBN, adding ΔN_eff≈1 and ~1 eV to Σm_ν. Planck's N_eff=2.99±0.17 and mass bounds exclude it unless self-interactions or lepton asymmetries suppress production; extra dark radiation as a Hubble-tension fix is proposed but disfavoured.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: keV sterile neutrinos as warm dark matter
summary: A keV sterile neutrino produced by oscillations (Dodelson–Widrow) or resonantly (Shi–Fuller) is warm dark matter whose free-streaming suppresses dwarf-scale power. Lyman-α and satellite counts combined with X-ray limits on ν_s→νγ exclude non-resonant production, and the claimed 3.5 keV line remains contested.

name: Effective field theory of inflation
summary: Inflationary perturbations are treated as the Goldstone mode π of broken time translations, with operators ordered by derivatives as in chiral perturbation theory. A reduced sound speed predicts f_NL^equil∝(1−c_s²)/c_s², and heavy fields leave oscillatory 'cosmological collider' signals in the squeezed bispectrum.
sources: Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)

name: EFT tower for dark-matter–nucleus scattering
summary: Direct-detection rates come from an EFT chain. Mediator-scale operators run down to quark and gluon operators, nucleon matrix elements (σ_πN, spin fractions) and chiral EFT match them to nucleons, and the result is a basis of Galilean-invariant non-relativistic operators — the same tower used for flavour physics and nuclear forces.
map: \mathcal O_1=1_\chi1_N,\ \mathcal O_4=\vec S_\chi\cdot\vec S_N,\ \dots\ \text{from}\ i\vec q,\ \vec v^{\perp},\ \vec S_\chi,\ \vec S_N
sources: Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)

name: Lattice QCD crossover in the early universe
summary: Lattice QCD shows the quark–hadron transition near 156 MeV is a smooth crossover, so it leaves no bubbles and no strong gravitational-wave signal. The lattice equation of state supplies g_*(T), and the topological susceptibility χ(T) feeds WIMP and axion relic-abundance calculations.
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)

name: Weak freeze-out sets neutrino decoupling and n/p
summary: Weak rates Γ≈G_F²T⁵ fall below the Hubble rate at T≈1 MeV, so neutrinos decouple. Electron–positron annihilation then heats the photons, giving T_ν=(4/11)^{1/3}T_γ and N_eff=3.044, and the frozen n/p≈1/7 fixes primordial helium Y_p≈0.25; the Fermi constant thereby shapes the expansion history.
sources: Weinberg (1967). "A Model of Leptons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 19, 1264. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1264](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1264)

name: Higgs inflation and electroweak vacuum stability
summary: With a large nonminimal coupling ξ|H|²R (ξ~10⁴), the measured Higgs can act as the inflaton and gives Starobinsky-like predictions n_s≈0.965 and r≈0.003. Conversely, the running Higgs quartic turns negative near 10¹⁰–10¹¹ GeV, so the metastable electroweak vacuum constrains the Hubble scale during inflation and reheating.
sources: Starobinsky (1980). "A new type of isotropic cosmological models without singularity". *Phys. Lett. B* 91, 99. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X)

name: Dense QCD and the neutron-star equation of state
summary: Neutron-star cores reach several times nuclear saturation density, where QCD is nonperturbative and lattice QCD fails because of the sign problem. Masses ≳2 M_⊙, NICER radii and GW170817 tidal deformability constrain the equation of state, testing hyperons, deconfined quark matter and colour superconductivity, while perturbative QCD bounds the high-density end.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)
Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)

name: Evaluated reaction-rate libraries for stellar models
summary: Stellar evolution and explosion codes use evaluated thermonuclear rate compilations (REACLIB, NACRE) built from nuclear data and Hauser-Feshbach theory, so evaluation and covariance methods from nuclear data propagate into stellar predictions.
breaks: Many network rates are theoretical; uncertainties are correlated and often lack covariance information.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2010). "The JINA REACLIB Database: Its Recent Updates and Impact on Type-I X-ray Bursts". *Astrophys. J. Suppl.* 189, 240. [doi:10.1088/0067-0049/189/1/240](https://doi.org/10.1088/0067-0049/189/1/240)

name: Low-background radiation detectors for dark matter
summary: Dark-matter direct detection uses nuclear-physics detector technology (scintillators, HPGe, noble-liquid ionization) and radiation-protection-grade background control; nuclear-recoil quenching and gamma/neutron backgrounds are nuclear-physics problems.

name: Nuclear radiation detectors as gamma-ray telescopes
summary: MeV gamma-ray astronomy (nuclear lines, GRBs) uses nuclear-spectroscopy detectors: NaI and BGO scintillators, HPGe spectrometers (INTEGRAL/SPI) and Compton telescopes, with the same photoelectric/Compton/pair physics and activation backgrounds.
breaks: Space instruments face cosmic-ray activation and must reject a large instrumental background.

name: PDFs set ultra-high-energy neutrino cross sections
summary: The neutrino-nucleon cross section above ~10 TeV is deep-inelastic scattering dominated by small-x sea quarks and gluons; IceCube's Earth-absorption measurement agrees with PDF-based predictions, and small-x uncertainty (and saturation) sets the high-energy event rate.
breaks: At the highest energies the relevant x lies below HERA's reach, so predictions extrapolate DGLAP or invoke saturation.
sources: IceCube Collaboration (2017). "Measurement of the multi-TeV neutrino interaction cross-section with IceCube using Earth absorption". *Nature* 551, 596. [arXiv:1711.08119](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08119)

name: QGP epoch of the early universe
summary: The universe was a quark-gluon plasma until ~10 microseconds, when it cooled through the QCD crossover at T_c ~ 156 MeV; heavy-ion collisions recreate that matter, and the lattice equation of state measured there fixes the early-universe expansion rate through that epoch.
breaks: Heavy-ion fireballs have mu_B > 0 at lower energies, are tiny and expand in ~10 fm/c, and are not in global equilibrium; the cosmic transition is at mu_B ~ 0 and expands over microseconds.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: Antinuclei: coalescence and absorption for dark matter
summary: Antideuterons and antihelium in cosmic rays would be a near background-free dark-matter signature; coalescence parameters measured in heavy-ion and pp collisions and ALICE's antihelium absorption cross sections set both the expected signal and the cosmic-ray background.
breaks: Coalescence depends on source size, which differs between Galactic dark-matter annihilation and collider systems.
sources: ALICE Collaboration (2023). "Measurement of anti-3He nuclei absorption in matter and impact on their propagation in the Galaxy". *Nature Phys.* 19, 61. [arXiv:2202.01549](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01549)

name: Quark-matter cores in massive neutron stars
summary: Model-agnostic EOS inference combining perturbative QCD at high density with nuclear EFT at low density finds the speed of sound and polytropic index in the cores of ~2-solar-mass stars consistent with deconfined quark matter.
breaks: The criterion is a heuristic; hadronic matter with a peaked sound speed can mimic it, so the claim is contested.
sources: Annala et al. (2020). "Evidence for quark-matter cores in massive neutron stars". *Nature Phys.* 16, 907. [arXiv:1903.09121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.09121)

name: Lattice QCD equation of state and early-universe g_*
summary: The lattice QCD equation of state and susceptibilities, tested against heavy-ion data, give the effective degrees of freedom g_*(T) and g_*s(T) through the QCD crossover, which enter relic-abundance and axion-density calculations.
breaks: Cosmic use needs mu_B ~ 0 and full equilibrium, where lattice QCD is reliable; heavy-ion data mainly validate it.
sources: Borsanyi et al. (2016). "Calculation of the axion mass based on high-temperature lattice quantum chromodynamics". *Nature* 539, 69. [arXiv:1606.07494](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07494)

name: QGP-like collectivity and the air-shower muon puzzle
summary: Air showers contain more muons than hadronic models predict; strangeness enhancement and core-corona collectivity seen in high-multiplicity LHC collisions, implemented in models such as EPOS, are candidate explanations, linking QGP signatures to cosmic-ray composition.
breaks: Air showers involve forward-rapidity, light-ion collisions beyond collider coverage, so the extrapolation is uncertain.
sources: Pierog et al. (2015). "EPOS LHC: Test of collective hadronization with data measured at the CERN Large Hadron Collider". *Phys. Rev. C* 92, 034906. [arXiv:1306.0121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0121)
ALICE Collaboration (2017). "Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton–proton collisions". *Nature Phys.* 13, 535. [arXiv:1606.07424](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07424)

name: Neutron-star mergers as nuclear laboratories
summary: Binary neutron-star mergers tie nuclear physics to multi-messenger signals: the EOS sets the inspiral tidal phase and remnant fate, and r-process nucleosynthesis powers the kilonova.
map: \tilde\Lambda\ \text{from GW phase}\ \leftrightarrow\ P(\varepsilon);\ L_{\rm KN}(t)\propto\dot\epsilon_{\rm r}(t)\approx t^{-1.3}
breaks: Mergers mix nuclear uncertainties with GR-MHD and neutrino transport uncertainties, so inferences are model-dependent.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)

name: Nuclear burning powers stars and builds elements
summary: Thermonuclear reaction rates set the luminosity, lifetime and composition of stars at every stage, from pp burning through silicon burning and explosive nucleosynthesis.
sources: Bethe (1939). "Energy Production in Stars". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 434. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.434](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.434)
Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Expansion rate versus weak freeze-out in BBN
summary: Primordial abundances are set where the Friedmann expansion rate overtakes the weak n-p conversion rate (T ~ 0.8 MeV) and the deuterium bottleneck opens (T ~ 0.07 MeV); BBN is therefore a test of cosmology at MeV temperatures, constraining N_eff and new physics.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Baryon density from BBN and CMB agree
summary: Deuterium from quasar absorbers gives Omega_b h^2 through BBN at ~1 percent, matching the CMB acoustic-peak value: two physically independent measurements of the same baryon-to-photon ratio, minutes and 380 kyr after the Big Bang.
breaks: The BBN value depends on nuclear rates (d(p,gamma)3He) and D/H systematics; the CMB value depends on the LambdaCDM fit.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)
Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: BBN tests the Friedmann equation at MeV temperatures
summary: BBN abundances measure the radiation-dominated expansion rate H(T) and g_*, testing the Friedmann equation and the relativistic-species content 1-1000 s after the Big Bang, the earliest direct probe of the expansion history.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: BBN plus BAO gives a CMB-independent H0
summary: Deuterium-calibrated BBN fixes the baryon density, which sets the sound horizon for BAO without CMB anisotropies; the resulting H0 agrees with Planck, so the Hubble tension is not a CMB-specific systematic. BBN also limits early-dark-energy and extra-radiation fixes through N_eff.
breaks: The result inherits LambdaCDM late-time assumptions and the d(p,gamma) rate uncertainty.
sources: Schöneberg, Lesgourgues & Hooper (2019). "The BAO+BBN take on the Hubble tension". *J. Cosmol. Astropart. Phys.* 10, 029. [arXiv:1907.11594](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.11594)
Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: BBN baryon budget demands non-baryonic dark matter
summary: BBN limits baryons to Omega_b ~ 0.05, while dynamics, lensing and the CMB need Omega_m ~ 0.3; most matter must therefore be non-baryonic, one of the strongest independent arguments for particle dark matter.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)
Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: Lithium problem: primordial or stellar depletion?
summary: Standard BBN predicts 7Li/H about three times the Spite plateau in metal-poor halo stars; whether the gap is nuclear (7Be destruction rates), stellar (atomic diffusion and mixing in stellar atmospheres) or new physics is unresolved, with stellar depletion now favoured.
sources: Fields (2011). "The Primordial Lithium Problem". *Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 61, 47. [arXiv:1203.3551](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3551)

name: Neutron stars as dark-matter detectors
summary: Dark matter captured by scattering on neutron-star nucleons would heat old neutron stars; the capture rate uses the same dark-matter-nucleon cross section as direct detection, with neutron-star nuclear matter and Pauli blocking replacing the target nucleus.
breaks: Capture in dense matter involves strong-interaction medium effects and relativistic kinematics, and no candidate star has been observed at the required temperature.
sources: Baryakhtar et al. (2017). "Dark Kinetic Heating of Neutron Stars and An Infrared Window On WIMPs, SIMPs, and Pure Higgsinos". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 131801. [arXiv:1704.01577](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01577)

name: Magnetar crusts: starquakes, QPOs and outbursts
summary: Magnetar bursts, giant flares and possibly FRBs are driven by crust stresses from evolving 1e15 G fields; crust breaking strain, shear modulus and seismic modes from nuclear and crust physics set burst energetics and QPO frequencies.
map: E_{\rm el}\sim\mu\,\epsilon_{\rm br}^2V_{\rm crust}/2;\ f_{\rm torsional}\approx\frac{v_t}{2\pi R}\sqrt{\ell(\ell+1)}\sim20\text{–}100\ \text{Hz}
breaks: Whether FRBs come from crust events or from magnetospheric or wind processes is unresolved.
sources: Kaspi & Beloborodov (2017). "Magnetars". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 55, 261. [arXiv:1703.00068](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00068)

name: Maximum mass from merger remnants and short GRBs
summary: Whether a merger remnant collapses promptly, after a delay, or survives as a magnetar depends on the maximum neutron-star mass; the GW170817 short GRB and kilonova energetics argued for delayed collapse, suggesting M_max of about 2.2-2.3 solar masses.
map: M_{\rm thr}\approx kM_{\rm max},\ k\sim1.3\text{–}1.7;\ M_{\rm TOV}\lesssim2.2\text{–}2.3\,M_\odot
breaks: The argument depends on interpreting the kilonova ejecta and jet energetics, which are model-dependent.
sources: Margalit & Metzger (2017). "Constraining the Maximum Mass of Neutron Stars from Multi-messenger Observations of GW170817". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 850, L19. [arXiv:1710.05938](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05938)

name: Tidal deformability from GW170817 constrains the EOS
summary: The GW170817 inspiral phase measured the binary tidal deformability, limiting neutron-star radii to ~11-13 km and excluding the stiffest nuclear EOS; joint analyses with NICER and nuclear data now bound pressure at twice saturation density.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)

name: Dense-matter EOS sets neutron-star masses and radii
summary: The TOV equation turns the nuclear EOS into a mass-radius curve; 2-solar-mass pulsars, NICER radii and GW tidal deformabilities constrain matter up to several times saturation density.
sources: Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

name: EOS in core collapse and proto-neutron stars
summary: Core bounce, proto-neutron-star contraction, neutrino-driven explosion and black-hole formation depend on the finite-temperature nuclear EOS (stiffness, symmetry energy, nuclear statistical equilibrium composition).
breaks: Supernova EOS tables need finite temperature and proton fraction 0.05-0.5, beyond the cold beta-equilibrium EOS of neutron stars.
sources: Janka et al. (2007). "Theory of core-collapse supernovae". *Phys. Rep.* 442, 38. [arXiv:astro-ph/0612072](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0612072)

name: Nucleosynthesis yields drive galactic chemical evolution
summary: Galaxy-formation simulations and chemical-evolution models use stellar and explosive yields (alpha elements from core collapse, Fe from Ia, s from AGB, r from mergers) as inputs; alpha/Fe ratios then clock star-formation histories.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Galactic archaeology of r-process-enhanced stars
summary: Europium-rich metal-poor halo stars, the actinide-boost class and the single-event enrichment of the dwarf galaxy Reticulum II test which sites (rare, prolific mergers or collapsars) made the Milky Way's r-process elements and when.
breaks: Merger delay times and natal kicks complicate the link between abundance trends and sites.
sources: Ji et al. (2016). "R-process enrichment from a single event in an ancient dwarf galaxy". *Nature* 531, 610. [arXiv:1512.01558](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01558)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

name: Magnetar giant flares as r-process sites
summary: Delayed MeV gamma-ray emission after the 2004 SGR 1806-20 giant flare matches radioactive decay of freshly synthesized r-process nuclei in baryon-loaded ejecta, suggesting magnetars contribute a few percent of the r-process.
breaks: Single-event evidence; the ejecta mass and Y_e are inferred from models.
sources: Patel et al. (2025). "Direct Evidence for r-process Nucleosynthesis in Delayed MeV Emission from the SGR 1806–20 Magnetar Giant Flare". *Astrophys. J. Lett.*. [arXiv:2501.09181](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09181)

name: Collapsars as r-process sites
summary: Neutron-rich accretion-disk outflows in collapsars (the engines of long GRBs) may make r-process material comparable to mergers, which would explain early-galaxy enrichment; near-infrared follow-up of long GRBs is testing this.
breaks: Disk-outflow Y_e depends on neutrino transport and magnetic physics that simulations do not yet agree on.
sources: Siegel, Barnes & Metzger (2019). "Collapsars as a major source of r-process elements". *Nature* 569, 241. [arXiv:1810.00098](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00098)

name: Kilonova AT2017gfo and r-process nucleosynthesis
summary: The optical-infrared kilonova after GW170817 was powered by radioactive decay of freshly made r-process nuclei, and its red component showed lanthanide-rich ejecta, the first direct identification of an r-process site.
map: \kappa_{\rm lanth}\sim10\ \text{cm}^2\text{g}^{-1}\gg\kappa_{\rm Fe};\ t_{\rm peak}\approx\sqrt{\frac{\kappa M}{4\pi vc}}
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)
Pian et al. (2017). "Spectroscopic identification of r-process nucleosynthesis in a double neutron star merger". *Nature* 551, 67. [arXiv:1710.05858](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05858)

name: s-process in AGB stars and barium/CEMP binaries
summary: Barium stars and carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP-s) stars got their s-process overabundances by mass transfer from an AGB companion, so binary populations map the s-process yields and neutron exposures of extinct AGB stars.
sources: Escorza et al. (2026). "Stellar nucleosynthesis in the era of large surveys: S-process polluted binaries in GALAH DR4". *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2604.15197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15197)

name: Stellar evolution drives s-process and burning stages
summary: Burning stages (H, He, C, Ne, O, Si) follow core contraction; thermal pulses in AGB stars release neutrons via 13C(alpha,n) and 22Ne(alpha,n) for the s-process, and the triple-alpha rate through the Hoyle state sets the C/O ratio.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Supernovae as nucleosynthesis sites
summary: Core-collapse supernovae make the alpha elements and iron-peak nuclei through explosive burning and the nu-p and weak r-process; thermonuclear (Ia) supernovae make most of the iron. Ordinary core-collapse ejecta fail to reach the third r-process peak.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

name: Urca processes and neutrino cooling of compact stars
summary: Neutron stars cool by direct and modified Urca beta processes whose rates depend on the proton fraction and pairing; accreting crusts hold Urca shells, and electron capture onto nuclei sets white-dwarf and crust compositions.
map: n\to pe\bar\nu_e,\ pe\to n\nu_e;\ \text{direct Urca if }x_p\gtrsim0.11;\ \epsilon_{\rm dU}\propto T^6,\ \epsilon_{\rm mU}\propto T^8
breaks: The proton fraction and pairing gaps in the core are uncertain, so cooling curves constrain them only jointly.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)
Dean & Hjorth-Jensen (2003). "Pairing in nuclear systems: from neutron stars to finite nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 607. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.75.607](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.75.607)

name: Electron capture and weak rates in core collapse
summary: Electron captures on iron-group and neutron-rich nuclei (Gamow-Teller strength from the shell model) deleptonize the collapsing core and set the homologous-core mass, shock energy and neutrino signal of core-collapse supernovae.
breaks: Gamow-Teller strength of hot, neutron-rich nuclei far from stability is only partly measured; tables extrapolate shell-model and QRPA results.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)

name: Deuterium burning separates brown dwarfs from planets
summary: The deuterium-burning mass limit (~13 Jupiter masses) is the conventional boundary between giant planets and brown dwarfs; it is set by when the core reaches the D(p,gamma)3He Gamow window before electron degeneracy halts contraction.
breaks: The limit depends on helium and deuterium fraction and metallicity; formation mode, not burning, may be the better planet criterion.
sources: Spiegel, Burrows & Milsom (2011). "The Deuterium-burning Mass Limit for Brown Dwarfs and Giant Planets". *Astrophys. J.* 727, 57. [arXiv:1008.5150](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.5150)

name: Gamow-peak fusion sets stellar structure
summary: Stellar energy generation is set by sub-barrier fusion at the Gamow peak; the steep temperature dependence of the CNO cycle versus pp chain decides convective cores and the main-sequence mass-luminosity relation.
sources: Bethe (1939). "Energy Production in Stars". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 434. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.434](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.434)
Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)

name: Carbon fusion rate and thermonuclear ignition
summary: Carbon ignition in white dwarfs (Type Ia supernovae), carbon flashes and X-ray superbursts depend on the low-energy 12C+12C fusion rate, whose resonant structure below 2 MeV remains uncertain.
breaks: Laboratory data stop above the Gamow window, and electron screening in dense plasmas modifies the rate.
sources: Tan et al. (2024). "Coincident measurement of the C12+C12 fusion cross section via the differential thick-target technique". *Phys. Rev. C* 110, 035808. [doi:10.1103/physrevc.110.035808](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevc.110.035808)

name: Solar neutrinos measure pp-chain and CNO burning
summary: Neutrino fluxes from the pp chain (pp, 7Be, 8B) and the first detection of CNO neutrinos test laboratory fusion cross sections in the solar core; the CNO flux bears on the solar metallicity (abundance) problem raised by helioseismology.
breaks: Interpreting fluxes needs neutrino oscillation (MSW) parameters and the solar model's opacities.
sources: Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)
Borexino Collaboration (2020). "Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun". *Nature* 587, 577. [arXiv:2006.15115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15115)

name: Fission yields shape r-process patterns and kilonovae
summary: Fission of the heaviest r-process nuclei recycles material to the second peak, shapes the rare-earth abundances and, through 254Cf, can dominate late-time kilonova heating; fission barriers and yields far from stability are a major r-process uncertainty.
breaks: Barriers and fragment yields of neutron-rich actinides come from models without measurements.
sources: Zhu et al. (2018). "Californium-254 and Kilonova Light Curves". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 863, L23. [arXiv:1806.09724](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.09724)

name: Coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering and the neutrino fog
summary: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, observed by COHERENT, gives nuclear recoils indistinguishable from WIMP signals; solar 8B and atmospheric neutrinos thus form the neutrino fog of direct detection, with rates set by the weak charge and neutron form factor.
breaks: The neutrino background is irreducible only for the same recoil spectrum; directionality and target complementarity partly separate it.
sources: COHERENT Collaboration (2017). "Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering". *Science* 357, 1123. [arXiv:1708.01294](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01294)

name: Cosmic-ray spallation and Li-Be-B production
summary: Spallation of cosmic-ray C, N, O on interstellar H and He makes Li, Be and B; secondary-to-primary ratios such as B/C measure the grammage traversed and calibrate Galactic propagation, so they rest on nuclear fragmentation cross sections.
breaks: Fragmentation cross sections are known to only 10-20 percent, which now limits AMS-02 propagation analyses.

name: Radioactive heating of kilonova ejecta
summary: Kilonovae are powered by the summed beta decays and fission of thousands of r-process nuclei, giving a heating rate close to t^-1.3; the luminosity therefore measures ejected r-process mass.
breaks: Thermalization efficiency and the uncertain beta-decay rates and masses of neutron-rich nuclei limit the mass inference to a factor of a few.
sources: Metzger et al. (2010). "Electromagnetic Counterparts of Compact Object Mergers Powered by the Radioactive Decay of R-process Nuclei". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 406, 2650. [arXiv:1001.5029](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.5029)
Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)

name: 26Al heating and chronometry of the early Solar System
summary: Excess 26Mg in meteoritic inclusions shows live 26Al (t1/2 = 0.72 Myr) was present when the first solids formed; its decay heat melted and differentiated planetesimals, and short-lived radionuclides give Myr-resolution chronologies of disk evolution.
breaks: Dating assumes 26Al was homogeneously distributed in the disk, which is debated.
sources: Lee, Papanastassiou & Wasserburg (1976). "Demonstration of 26Mg excess in Allende and evidence for 26Al". *Geophys. Res. Lett.* 3, 41. [doi:10.1029/GL003i001p00041](https://doi.org/10.1029/GL003i001p00041)

name: Radioactive 56Ni-56Co decay powers supernova light curves
summary: Type Ia and stripped-envelope supernova light curves are powered by 56Ni -> 56Co -> 56Fe decay (6.1 d and 77 d), so the peak luminosity measures the nickel mass (Arnett's rule) and the tail follows the cobalt half-life; 44Ti maps in Cas A trace explosion asymmetry.
map: ^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\xrightarrow{6.1\,\rm d}{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\xrightarrow{77\,\rm d}{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe};\ L_{\rm peak}\approx\dot E_{\rm Ni}(t_{\rm peak});\ L_{\rm tail}\propto e^{-t/111\,\rm d}
breaks: Gamma-ray escape and positron trapping make the deposited luminosity differ from the decay luminosity at late times.
sources: Grefenstette et al. (2014). "Asymmetries in core-collapse supernovae from maps of radioactive 44Ti in CassiopeiaA". *Nature* 506, 339. [arXiv:1403.4978](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.4978)
